claims.statement: The W3 boot sequence (01_boot_online.boot_sequence) runs in the finalized order: load the week plan (T1-lite plan_loader; missing/conflicting files fall back to self-learning mode), persist the plan to dss.dim_weekly_plan (failure reported, non-fatal), check existence of the 14 dss learning tables (read-only information_schema), run the derive_postexit_stations gate whose mismatch only enters the boot report without auto-changing the POST_EXIT_STATIONS constant, run the 120h bootstrap replay plus cross_check, run the FreshnessGuard first check (stale data at boot is declared immediately, not masked), and render the boot report echoing all effective configuration values.

In replay_cursor mode main() requires DSS_REPLAY_START/DSS_REPLAY_END env (ISO) and anchors the bootstrap's now to the replay start (agy T2.6 中①): anchoring to the wall clock would pin the watermark at the current table max ID and make the whole replay consume nothing.

run_one_round has the frozen round order shared by wall_clock and replay_cursor modes: consume(now, pool) -> frozen = guard.check(now, stream.front) (the sole guard.check call point per round) -> dead = pool.dead_sweep(now, frozen) (always called; freeze semantics absorbed inside the sweep, never by caller-side skipping) -> record_dead_audit + conn.commit() only when dead is non-empty -> status dict {now, pool_size, max_ts, guard_state, guard_label, frozen, dead_count}.

F8 watermark discipline: the incremental EventStream starts at BootstrapReport.watermark (the maximum row ID of the 120h replay window; main also sets stream.front = data_max_ts), set_watermark is up-only so the start point never regresses, and meta.refresh_watermark is the ETL-layer watermark used only for B3 S2 diagnosis — never the DSS start watermark; there is no local state file (state is purely reconstructed from the event stream).
boot_sequence raises RuntimeError and aborts startup when BootstrapReport.watermark == 0 (no data in the replay window): the incremental stream must never start from 0 (F8).

EventStream.consume pulls rows with a single query FROM ods.carbody_history WHERE "ID" > wm AND "DATE_EVT" <= now ORDER BY "ID" (flag = SUBSTRING(MDS_DATA FROM 139 FOR 1), flag137 = bit 137 extracted in SQL); the :now upper bound is mandatory — in replay_cursor mode events with ts > now are not pulled this round so the watermark never advances past the cursor (without it the first replay round would pull the whole ~6.33M-row table), and in wall_clock mode the condition is a constant true no-op.

After fetching, consume dispatches rows in (ts, ID) ascending order (F-1② fix, 2026-09-25): real data shows ~52% ID/ts inversion, and ID-order dispatch misfired the in-window-late path after front advanced, causing ~136k per-car log subqueries (~200k over a 7-day/2016-round replay ≈ 11h, infeasible); ts-ordered dispatch makes front advance monotonically while the skew split remains the safety net for genuine late arrivals.

Skew three-way split per event (skew_window_min default 15): ts >= front (in order) -> normal ingest and front advance; front − skew_window <= ts < front (late in window) -> _replay_late issues a per-car log query (WHERE "BODY_ID" = :b AND "DATE_EVT" BETWEEN since AND now ORDER BY DATE_EVT,ID; since = entry_ts full-cycle for in-pool cars, now − 24h cap for out-of-pool cars) and calls pool.replay_car; ts < front − skew_window -> audit["late_out_of_window"] += 1 with pool state untouched (daily reconcile backstop).

replay_car recompute merge rule: the per-car slice is replayed through the same R1/R2/R6 state machine from a fresh position; station/flag/loop_count/last_event_ts are set to the recompute result while entry_ts/exits_seen stay untouched (lifecycle counts come from in-order events only); a latest slice event at an exit or post-exit station removes in-pool cars and does not adopt out-of-pool cars; _seen_row_ids row_id dedup (bounded 256) makes recomputation idempotent (no duplicate audit counts), and station-level ts merge takes max over the slice.

FreshnessGuard.check is pure computation advancing a three-state machine with a two-fresh latch: NORMAL -> STALE when lag >= stale_min (default 30min); STALE -> RECOVERY on the first fresh check (transitional, not frozen); RECOVERY -> NORMAL on the second consecutive fresh check and back to STALE if stale again; every transition is appended to the guard log as (time, "OLD->NEW"); max_event_ts=None is treated as infinite lag -> conservative STALE.

STALE-only freeze semantics (B3 final): only status STALE makes check return frozen=True; the frozen objects are alerts plus the dead-car sweep, while pool consumption and prediction computation are NOT frozen (consume/ETA keep advancing so post-line-stop data backflow cannot desync); RECOVERY/NORMAL never freeze.

expected_silence rest-day downgrade (P2 clause): on rest days the guard still goes STALE and still returns frozen, but the label degrades to 「无数据属预期」 and is_anomaly is False (not counted as anomaly/acceptance); with expected_silence=False the same lag yields label 「数据陈旧」 and is_anomaly=True.

FreshnessGuard.diagnose reads four signals (S1 last meta.sync_job_log run of ETL job refresh_carbody_ods; S2 meta.refresh_watermark ods.carbody_history.max_id vs full-table MAX(ID) gap; S3 MAX(DATE_EVT) of ods.carbody_history; S4 MAX(vehicle_updated_at) of ods.rb_position_data) and returns the BM verdict: event fresh (S3 lag < stale_min) -> 「新鲜」 with ETL signals diagnostic only; events stopped + ETL unhealthy -> 「断流」; events stopped + ETL healthy (S1 success and lag < lag_min, S2 gap = 0, S4 lag < lag_min) -> 「移交模式A」 (genuine line stop handed to B7 station-level whitelist judgment).

R1: entry at any of the 3 ENTRY_STATIONS enters/updates the pool; consecutive same-station events are idempotent updates (last_event_ts refreshed, same_station_dups audit count incremented, loop_count unchanged) and events are never dropped by a time window — real adjacent fast passes (~18.2%) must be kept.
R2: invalid flags {'-','3'} inherit the last valid flag and must never reset it to 0 (valid flags = {'0','1','2'}); every invalid-flag event increments the per-car invalid_flags audit counter.

R3: the first exit of the current period at any of the 4 EXIT_STATIONS removes the car from the pool and increments the exits audit; re-entry at an entry station starts a new period (flag = that event's valid value, entry_ts reset, loop_count = 0, loop_exited reset False); exit events for cars not in the pool (exits_seen >= 2) are audit-only and do not touch the pool.

R4 mid-line adoption with double ghost-car insurance (2026-09-24 incident): an out-of-pool car with a non-entry, non-exit station event enters the pool immediately (entry_ts = that event ts); the dynamic history lock absolutely forbids adoption of a car with exits_seen > 0 at any non-entry station (line-head re-entry must pass an entry station); and the static POST_EXIT_STATIONS set (09IS360, 09IS350, K3IS230, K2IS165, K1IS225) is audit-only and silent for out-of-pool cars (not counted as exits) while triggering pool removal for in-pool cars.

R5: body_type is taken directly from the DB column BODY_TYPE (same source as W1 tmp_ev_base.bt) with no BODY_ID prefix derivation; NULL falls back to an empty string and never crashes; pull SQL must include the column.

R6: loop_count increments by 1 only on a non-consecutive re-pass of a station already visited in the current period; consecutive same-station runs do not count (R1), and re-passing an entry station resets the counter for the new period.

R7 timezone hard constraint: a single DSN connection runs SET TIME ZONE 'Asia/Shanghai' so all DB timestamps arrive +08:00 aware on the Asia/Shanghai baseline; every datetime is required aware — a naive ts raises TypeError at pool and loop entry points (ingest, consume, check, diagnose, bootstrap, dead_sweep, reconcile, main-loop start/end), machine-enforced rather than documented.

Per-car W4.3c trajectory fields: passed_oven (O1) is set True monotonically when the car passes an oven-out station (eta_v2.OVEN_OUT_STATIONS single source of truth) and is never reset — only whole-VehicleState deletion clears it; flag_137 (O2) follows the car as the latest event's 137-bit value with '-' / NULL normalized to '0' (_norm137) and follows only that car's own trajectory (no cross-car contamination).

loop_exited (W4.4c (α), Doc14 v1.4 R3' loop-exit guard): set True when the car passes any of the three 25IS010/110/210 gateway exits (eta_v2.LOOP_EXIT_GATEWAYS); it is reset to False only on the new-period signal (re-passing an entry station); mainline residual-bit events do not reset it because the MES bit never clearing is a data fact.

last_event_by_station returns each station's most recent pass-event ts with station-level retention: the timestamp survives the car leaving or the pool emptying, every ingest event updates it (including audit-only exit events) under max semantics, and B7 line-stop sensing depends on it to distinguish a car that just left from a station silent for longer than the threshold.

M7 dead-car semantics: dead_sweep (frozen signature, no conn) removes and reports cars with no new event since their last event for >= dead_vehicle_hours (default 120h, injected via the constructor from cfg.dead_vehicle_hours; tests compress the threshold, e.g. 1h); frozen=True (B3 STALE) makes the sweep a no-op; a new event on a dead car auto-revives it via R4 adoption with entry_ts = new event ts; removals clear _vehicles + _visited as a pair but deliberately keep _seen_row_ids so later skew-late recomputes cannot double-count dup/invalid audit on old row_ids.

Dead-car audit persistence lives in the orchestration layer: record_dead_audit(conn, dead, now) returns 0 for an empty list, otherwise lazily creates dss.work_alert_log (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, 6 columns) and INSERTs one row per dead car with the type literal 'dead_car' (since = last event ts, detected_at = judgment moment); writes go to the dss schema only while ods/dim/fct/mart/meta remain read-only.

_rebuild (F-1 self-healing primitive) first builds a shadow pool via a fresh VehiclePool bootstrap over the 120h window using the same state machine, and only on success swaps its internal structures (_vehicles, _visited, _station_last_event_ts, _seen_row_ids, audit) into the main pool atomically — a bootstrap failure mid-way keeps the old pool intact and propagates the exception, never leaving an empty pool (agy T2.6 低①) — then advances the watermark up-only and sets stream.front = report.data_max_ts.

Both wall_clock and replay_cursor modes run a periodic full rebuild every rebuild_hours (env DSS_REBUILD_HOURS, default 24h), and run_replay additionally rebuilds once at the end point so the replay terminal state equals the pure-bootstrap truth (acceptance anchor); this is the fix for the F-1 incident (watermark skip lost 0.37% of rows on day 1; a real watermark-poisoning case lost ~11h of data during which B3 reported STALE for 203 rounds), bounding residual row loss to one rebuild interval.

cross_check compares the pool against the dim.dim_vehicle_profile reference set (vehicles seen within [now − hours, now] whose carbody_last_rw_station is not in the 4 exit + 5 post-exit stations) and returns the symmetric-difference count and pct = diff / max(pool, ref); > 1% is the DoD gate that puts a warning in the boot report (人工核对, 不自动修); at historical replay acceptance points the dim table (a present-state snapshot) is structurally invalid (F-2), so acceptance switches to GT-SQL truth comparison.

The production wall_clock loop polls every poll_interval_sec (default 300s) with now = wall clock aware, and sleeps with next_grid_wait — a pure function computing the wait to the next epoch grid point ((int(ts) // poll + 1) * poll, lower bound 1.0s against busy-spin) — so frame timestamps land on the 5-minute grid (:00/:05/.../:55) with drift compensation (M5 anchor-frame preparation, agy 阻断 F2).

Two-value binding (B4 point 7): when DSS_BOOTSTRAP_HOURS is not explicitly set, bootstrap_hours takes the dead_vehicle_hours value, so changing only the dead threshold follows into the bootstrap window (tests monkeypatch to verify).

load_rest_days in 01_boot_online is a frozen compatibility shim (delegating to plan_loader.parse_csv(...).rest_days(), rest-day semantics = day+mid shift both 休) that the frozen 02/03 replayers call via dynamic module loading; it must not be deleted even after T1 wiring (agy 中 M3 zero-change red line for docs/02/03 consumers).

reconcile(conn, now, pool, days=7) pulls 7 days of product-car events, feeds a clean pool in ts order, and compares vehicle sets plus per-car station/flag against the live pool, returning ReconcileReport(pool_size, only_in_live, only_in_fresh, state_mismatches); differences > 0 are written to the startup/inspection report and are never auto-repaired (manual judgment, audit trail).

Single state machine (B4): online consumption and bootstrap replay feed the same VehiclePool.ingest with no second logic; bootstrap additionally feeds events in (BODY_ID, ts, ID) ascending order with pure ingest (per-car independent state machine; a complete replay window has no late-event concept — skew routing is exclusive to the incremental stream; feeding by ID order measured 52% ts inversion and would have triggered ~136k per-car subqueries / 15min timeout, while pure ingest processes 260k rows in seconds).
